title: Review: Diffraction grating; Thin-film interference; Photons and the photoelectric effect; Wave–particle duality
source: Questions copied unchanged from the mission-lesson scripts for AP Physics 2 (status of the source: mission-lesson scripts of Oct-Nov 2026 (reviewed by AI reviewers; not signed off by a person)). Terms and clues: Q01-1#t4 term and clue written for the game; Q03-1#t3 term and clue written for the game; Q03-1#t1 term and clue written for the game; W09-1#t4 term and clue written for the game. Questions: Q01-1#N.13, Q03-1#N.7b, W09-1#N.4b, W15-1#N.11, Q01-1#N.4b, Q03-1#N.4b, W09-1#N.6, W15-1#N.6, Q01-1#N.9b, Q03-1#N.17a, W09-1#N.10, W15-1#N.10. Some questions repeat from the worlds it reviews.

assemble.prompt: Match each term to its definition.

items.label: Planck constant
items.clue: Symbol h: the energy of one quantum of light divided by its f; 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s.

items.label: Electron diffraction
items.clue: Bright concentric rings on a fluorescent screen after a beam passes through thin graphite.

items.label: Wave–particle duality
items.clue: Idea that light and matter each need two models, and the experiment decides which one shows.

items.label: Path difference
items.clue: Extra distance d sin θ for light from the next opening; a whole number of λ gives a bright beam.

questions.stem: Light whose photons each have energy 4.0 eV shines on three metals: X, with work function 2.0 eV; Y, with work function 3.0 eV; and Z, with work function 4.5 eV. Which statement about the maximum kinetic energy of the electrons emitted from each metal is correct?

options.text: Z's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and X's electrons the least
X's electrons have the greatest maximum kinetic energy, and Z emits no electrons
All three metals emit electrons, each with the same maximum kinetic energy
Their maximum kinetic energies cannot be ranked without the light's intensity

questions.stem: An electron's speed is reduced to one-third of its original value. Its speed is always much less than the speed of light. How does its de Broglie wavelength change?

options.text: It becomes three times as long.
It becomes one-third as long.
It becomes nine times as long.
It stays the same length.

questions.stem: Light of wavelength 600 nm is incident normally on a diffraction grating that has 800 lines per millimeter. At what angle from the normal is the second-order maximum?

A soap film (n = 1.33) in air is lit at normal incidence by green light of wavelength 532 nm in air. Two regions of the film have thicknesses of 100 nm and 200 nm. Which comparison of the light reflected from the two regions, with its reasoning, is correct?

options.text: Brighter at 100 nm, where the film has less pigment to absorb the green
Brighter at 200 nm, where the path difference is one wavelength in the film
Brighter at 200 nm, where the thicker film reflects more of the light
Brighter at 100 nm, where the two reflected waves arrive in phase

questions.stem: Light with a wavelength of 500 nm in air passes from the air into water (n = 1.33). What is the energy of each photon while it travels through the water? Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J s and c = 3.00 × 10⁸ m s⁻¹, and treat the speed of light in air as c.
An electron (mass 9.11 × 10⁻³¹ kg) in an electron microscope moves at 2.5 × 10⁷ m/s. Relativistic effects are negligible. What is its de Broglie wavelength? Use h = 6.63 × 10⁻³⁴ J·s.

Predict first. Monochromatic light is incident normally first on a double slit and then on a diffraction grating whose adjacent slits have the same separation d as the double slit. Every slit is equally illuminated. Compared with the double-slit fringes, how do the grating's principal maxima appear?

options.text: Farther apart than the fringes, because the grating has many more slits
At the same angles, but wider and dimmer, as the light is shared among more slits
Identical in position, width and brightness, because only d and λ matter
At the same angles as the double-slit fringes, but much sharper and brighter

questions.stem: A soap film (n = 1.33) in air is 115 nm thick. Light strikes it at normal incidence. What is the longest wavelength, measured in air, for which the light reflected from the film's two surfaces interferes constructively?

options.text: 306 nm
460 nm
346 nm
612 nm

questions.stem: For a certain metal, the threshold frequency corresponds to light of wavelength 540 nm. Which of the following will eject electrons from the metal?

options.text: Red light of wavelength 650 nm from a bright lamp
Orange light of wavelength 600 nm left on for hours
Infrared radiation of wavelength 1200 nm from a lamp
Violet light of wavelength 410 nm from a very dim lamp

questions.stem: Electrons in a beam each have a de Broglie wavelength of 1.2 × 10⁻¹⁰ m. In which situation is quantum theory necessary to describe how the electrons behave?

options.text: When they pass through a slit 1.0 mm wide that is cut in a thin metal sheet
When they pass between rows of atoms in a crystal, 2.0 × 10⁻¹⁰ m apart
When they pass a pollen grain 2.0 × 10⁻⁵ m across, visible only by microscope
When they move through empty space at their speed of 6.1 × 10⁶ m/s

questions.stem: A laser beam is directed normally at a grating with 500 lines per mm. On a screen 1.00 m from the grating, the two second-order spots are 1.50 m apart. What is the wavelength of the laser light?

options.text: 750 nm
600 nm
832 nm

questions.stem: A camera lens has an antireflection coating designed for green light, so much less green light is reflected from it than from an uncoated lens. What happens to the energy of the green light that is no longer reflected?

options.text: It is destroyed where the two reflected waves interfere destructively.
It is absorbed by the coating, which warms up slightly as a result.
It is scattered off to the sides, so it does not come back to the viewer.
It is transmitted into the lens, so more green light reaches the camera's sensor.
